invariants.text: Export is read-only: opening, reading, timing out, disconnecting, resuming, and resynchronizing never claim, resolve, readdress, mutate, or delete an outbox intent or organizational record.
Every successful response is authenticated and authorized for its exact source_id before any event bytes are disclosed.
Every record carries the exact persisted DomainEvent bytes plus their SHA-256 digest and byte length; parsed metadata never substitutes for those bytes.
EventID is the deduplication identity. Delivery is at-least-once; reconnect and resynchronization may repeat an EventID and must not silently omit an eligible event.

An export cursor is opaque, integrity-protected, source-bound, principal-bound operational state. It never defines event identity, organizational order, causality, authority, acceptance, or completion.
Initial convergence opens the live observation boundary before reading bounded backlog.
Invalid, mismatched, tampered, expired, or history-lost cursor state never falls through to an apparently continuous stream; the response is RESYNC_REQUIRED or a closed failure.
After RESYNC_REQUIRED, a consumer opens a fresh live boundary before replaying bounded backlog and deduplicates all repeated EventIDs.
Each operation has a caller deadline, a server limit no greater than 1000 records, a wait no greater than 30 seconds, and observable terminal status.
Telemetry is content-free: it may include counts, durations, status, source identity, cursor digest, event digest, and byte length, but not payload, prompt, response, secret, or event bytes.
The source contract identity and exact source manifest SHA-256 accompany every successful response.
The export boundary does not interpret payload meaning and does not upconvert an event into organizational truth beyond the immutable event record itself.
